blocks.text: Fashion Business & Merchandising

A Fashion Buyer selects the clothing, footwear, accessories, and other fashion products that a retail business will sell. Buyers study consumer preferences, fashion trends, sales data, pricing, supplier capabilities, and profit margins to decide what products to purchase, in what quantities, and at what time.
The role combines fashion awareness with commercial judgment, negotiation, budgeting, inventory planning, and data analysis.
Product selection and trend forecasting
Identify suitable styles, fabrics, colors, silhouettes, price points, and collections for the target customer.
Supplier sourcing and negotiation
Work with manufacturers, brands, and vendors to negotiate prices, lead times, quality requirements, and order quantities.
Commercial and inventory planning
Use sales performance, margins, stock levels, and customer demand to improve assortment decisions and reduce excess inventory.

blocks.text: Career progression varies by retailer, category size, and the extent of commercial responsibility.
Suggested eight-semester plan for a B.Sc. in Fashion & Apparel. Adapt the roadmap to the institution's curriculum and available retail or industry placements.
Year 1 — Fashion and textile foundations
Semesters 1–2

items.text: Study fashion fundamentals, textile science, fibers, yarns, and fabric construction.
Learn garment types, silhouettes, fit, sizing, and basic garment manufacturing.
Understand color theory, fashion history, and consumer preferences.
Explore the apparel value chain, from design and sourcing to retail.
Learn Excel fundamentals and basic business calculations.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Create a fabric and apparel product catalogue with target customers, material details, and indicative price segments.
Year 2 — Merchandising and retail buying
Semesters 3–4

items.text: Learn fashion merchandising, retail operations, and assortment planning.
Study product costing, retail pricing, markups, markdowns, and gross margin.
Understand purchase orders, supplier quotations, lead times, and minimum order quantities.
Practice Excel formulas, pivot tables, lookups, and sales analysis.
Study consumer behavior, market segmentation, and competitor analysis.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Prepare a seasonal assortment plan for a hypothetical casualwear or ethnicwear collection.
Year 3 — Sourcing, planning, and commercial analysis
Semesters 5–6

items.text: Learn vendor evaluation, supplier negotiation, sourcing, and quality requirements.
Study demand forecasting, open-to-buy planning, inventory turnover, and stock availability.
Understand garment specifications, sampling, production timelines, and delivery coordination.
Explore Power BI or a similar tool for retail reporting.
Learn basic sustainability, ethical sourcing, and supply-chain traceability.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Build a buying plan with product-level sales forecasts, supplier comparisons, budget allocations, and margin calculations.

items.text: Apply for internships in buying, merchandising, sourcing, or retail planning.

blocks.text: Year 4 — Industry readiness and buying strategy
Semesters 7–8

items.text: Develop a complete seasonal buying strategy for a defined customer segment.
Analyze sales, sell-through, returns, markdowns, and inventory risks.
Practice supplier scorecards and product-performance reviews.
Understand purchase-order tracking, delivery schedules, and stock replenishment.
Complete an industry internship or retail buying research project.
Prepare a portfolio with assortment plans, costing sheets, dashboards, and supplier evaluation frameworks.
Practice commercial case studies and interviews for assistant buyer or merchandising roles.

blocks.text: Fashion and product knowledge
Essential
Fabrics, fibers, garment construction, fit, sizing, silhouettes, quality, and product specifications.
Trend and consumer analysis
Essential
Trend research, customer segmentation, competitor reviews, seasonal direction, and product relevance.
Commercial buying
Essential
Product selection, pricing, purchase quantities, assortment width and depth, budgets, and margin targets.
Retail mathematics
Essential
Markup, markdown, gross margin, sell-through, stock turnover, average selling price, and open-to-buy calculations.
Excel and data analysis
Essential
Formulas, pivot tables, lookups, conditional formatting, sales reports, and inventory tracking.
Supplier sourcing and negotiation
High priority
Vendor comparison, quotations, MOQ, lead times, payment terms, quality requirements, and delivery coordination.
Communication and collaboration
Essential
Negotiating with suppliers and coordinating with design, merchandising, quality, logistics, and retail teams.
Sustainability and compliance
Important
Material traceability, ethical sourcing, durability, waste reduction, and relevant product or market requirements.
Important buying and merchandising metrics

rows.text: Profitability of products before relevant operating expenses
How much of the available or received stock has sold during a period
How efficiently inventory is sold and replenished
Average realized selling price per unit sold
The extent to which products require price reductions
Remaining purchasing budget available for a period
Which variants customers buy and which remain in stock
How frequently products are returned and possible product issues

blocks.text: Definitions and calculation methods can vary by company, so always follow the retailer's reporting conventions.
Microsoft Excel
Your first priority for assortment planning, pricing, sales analysis, purchase orders, inventory reports, and budgeting.
Microsoft Power BI
Build dashboards for category performance, sales trends, margins, stock levels, and supplier performance.
Trend research platforms and fashion reports
Use available industry reports, runway analysis, retail observations, social trends, and customer data to support product decisions.
ERP and merchandising systems
Understand how retailers manage product master data, purchasing, inventory, supplier orders, and financial information. Specific systems depend on the employer.
Other useful tools include Google Sheets, PowerPoint, product lifecycle management (PLM) systems, inventory management software, and basic SQL for larger retail datasets.

blocks.label: Recommended approach
blocks.text: Master Excel first, then add Power BI and learn the purchasing or ERP system used by your target employer.
Create three projects that demonstrate your ability to make commercial buying decisions.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Seasonal fashion assortment plan
Beginner

items.text: Select a target customer and retail segment.
Choose products, categories, colors, sizes, and price bands.
Explain why each product belongs in the collection.
Create an assortment matrix with indicative quantities and prices.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A seasonal buying presentation, product catalogue, and Excel assortment plan.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Retail sales and inventory analysis
Intermediate

items.text: Analyze a public or simulated apparel sales dataset.
Calculate gross margin, sell-through, markdowns, and inventory turnover.
Identify high-performing and underperforming product categories.
Recommend replenishment, markdown, or assortment changes.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: An Excel analysis or Power BI dashboard with a concise commercial recommendation report.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Supplier sourcing and buying budget
Advanced

items.text: Compare hypothetical suppliers by price, quality, capacity, MOQ, and lead time.
Build a seasonal buying budget and product-level costing model.
Evaluate supplier risks and delivery constraints.
Explain how the chosen assortment supports margin and customer needs.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A supplier scorecard, costing workbook, purchasing recommendation, and risk assessment.
Final-year capstone recommendation
Data-Driven Fashion Buying and Assortment Planning System
Develop a buying strategy for a fashion category such as women's casualwear, menswear, footwear, or ethnicwear.
Include:

items.text: Target customer profile and competitor analysis.
Seasonal trend research and product selection.
Assortment planning by category, color, and size.
Product cost, retail price, and gross margin calculations.
Buying budget and open-to-buy planning.
Supplier evaluation and lead-time risk analysis.
Sales and inventory dashboard.
Recommendations for replenishment, markdowns, and future collections.

blocks.text: Use real data where available and label assumptions clearly when using simulated sales, supplier quotes, or forecasts.

rows.text: Excel, Power BI, and business analytics
Fashion references, garment details, and industry learning materials
Trend forecasting and consumer insights, where access is available
Fashion and lifestyle trend research, subject to subscription access
Retail analytics, supply chain, business, and data analysis courses

blocks.text: Optional certifications in retail merchandising, supply chain, Excel, or Power BI can support your profile. Choose courses based on relevance to the jobs you intend to pursue, and verify current fees and availability.
A postgraduate qualification is optional for many fashion buying careers.

items.text: M.Sc. in Fashion Merchandising or Fashion Management: deeper study of product planning, buying, and retail operations.
MBA in Retail Management or Fashion Management: useful for later category leadership, commercial strategy, and management roles.
Postgraduate programs in Supply Chain Management: useful for sourcing, procurement, and inventory planning.

blocks.label: Specialized training in retail analytics
blocks.text: helpful for data-intensive buying roles.
For a buying career, industry internships, commercial experience, supplier exposure, and analytical ability can be as important as additional qualifications.
Luxury and Premium Buying
Focus on premium labels, customer preferences, collection selection, price positioning, and brand relationships.
Fast Fashion and High-Volume Retail
Specialize in rapid product cycles, trend responsiveness, assortment breadth, replenishment, and inventory turnover.
Sustainable Fashion Buying
Focus on material traceability, supplier practices, product durability, responsible sourcing, and waste reduction.
E-commerce and Digital Buying
Use online sales, search behavior, product conversion, returns, and inventory data to optimize digital assortments.
Sourcing and Vendor Management
Focus on manufacturing partners, costing, quality, delivery timelines, capacity, and supply-chain risk.

blocks.label: AI-assisted trend analysis
blocks.text: using digital tools to organize product, customer, and trend information.

blocks.label: Data-driven assortment planning
blocks.text: using sales and inventory data to inform product selection and quantity decisions.

blocks.label: Omnichannel retail
blocks.text: coordinating product availability across stores, websites, and marketplaces.

blocks.label: Demand forecasting
blocks.text: improving purchase quantities and reducing stockouts or excess stock.

blocks.label: Digital product development
blocks.text: integrating digital samples and 3D garment visualization into product workflows.

blocks.label: Sustainability and traceability
blocks.text: evaluating sourcing transparency, material choices, and product life cycles.

blocks.label: Personalized retail
blocks.text: adapting assortments to customer segments, locations, and purchasing behavior.
AI and forecasting tools can support decisions, but buyers still need to validate data, understand the customer, assess supplier constraints, and exercise commercial judgment.
Priority 1 — Apparel and product knowledge
Understand fabrics, garment construction, fit, quality, and customer needs.
Priority 2 — Retail math and Excel
Practice costing, gross margin, markdowns, sales analysis, and buying budgets.
Priority 3 — Assortment and inventory planning
Learn how to choose products and quantities using demand, sales, and stock information.
Priority 4 — Sourcing and commercial communication
Practice supplier comparison, negotiation scenarios, and clear buying recommendations.
A graduate prepared for entry-level buying and merchandising roles should be able to:

items.text: Explain fabric, garment, fit, and quality considerations.
Research fashion trends and translate them into a target-customer assortment.
Prepare a seasonal product range and buying budget.
Calculate retail prices, margins, markdowns, and sell-through.
Analyze sales and inventory data in Excel.
Build a basic retail performance dashboard.
Compare suppliers using price, quality, MOQ, and lead time.
Understand purchase orders and product delivery workflows.
Present commercial recommendations supported by data.
Demonstrate these abilities through an assortment plan, analytical project, and buying portfolio.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Build your foundation around fashion product knowledge + retail mathematics + Excel + assortment planning. Then add supplier sourcing, inventory forecasting, and Power BI. A portfolio that demonstrates both fashion judgment and commercial analysis can help distinguish you from candidates who focus only on trends or design.
